turnaround_reason: Gogo provides in-flight broadband connectivity to business and commercial aviation. Stock crushed from $13 to $3.58 after heavy debt load, flat revenue, and a severe Q2 2026 earnings miss (-65% surprise). High short interest (15%) reflects skepticism, but real recurring revenue base and analyst targets at $8.50 suggest asymmetric setup if debt can be managed and growth re-accelerates.
bullish_points: Real operating business with $903M TTM revenue and 14% operating margins
Analyst consensus target $8.50 (2 analysts) vs current $3.58 — 137% upside
High short interest (15.4% float) creates potential squeeze fuel on any positive catalyst
Aviation connectivity is sticky recurring revenue; switching costs high once installed
Near 52-week lows with forward PE of 5.8x suggests deeply discounted valuation
bearish_points: Extremely leveraged: $880M debt vs $66M cash, debt/equity >700%
Q2 2026 earnings miss was severe (-65% vs estimates); guidance risk elevated
Revenue growth negative (-1.4% YoY) — needs to prove re-acceleration
Free cash flow negative (-$41M TTM) despite positive operating cash flow
Only 2 analysts covering; low institutional visibility post-downturn
catalyst: Q3 2026 earnings (Nov 5) + potential debt refinancing or strategic review announcements
catalyst_timing: Q3 earnings November 5 2026; any interim creditor or M&A chatter
suggested_trade: Small spot starter near current levels ($3.40-3.60), size 1-2% portfolio max. Add on volume confirmation above $4.50.
key_risk: Further debt covenant breach or continued revenue erosion leading to dilutive equity raise
would_skip_if: Further deterioration in liquidity metrics or missed Q3 estimates by >30%
